cards.text: Friend, this one starts quiet, so Papa's keeping his voice down for once. It's about Sarah, Abraham's wife, and the end of a long, long life.

cards.question: How old does Sarah, Abraham's wife, live to be?

cards.text: She dies in Kiriath-arba, that's Hebron, in the land of Canaan, and Abraham goes out to mourn and to weep for her. Then he gets up from beside her and goes to speak to the Hittites, the people living in that land.

cards.question: Abraham calls himself a foreigner and an outsider among the Hittites. He asks them to give him a ___ site among them.

cards.text: Abraham just called himself an outsider. But the Hittites answer him, “Listen to us, sir. You are God’s chosen one among us.”

cards.question: What do the Hittites offer Abraham so he can bury Sarah?

cards.text: Abraham rises and bows down before the Hittites. Then he asks them to go to Ephron son of Zohar for him about one spot: the cave of Machpelah, at the end of Ephron's field.

cards.question: Abraham wants Ephron to sell him the cave of Machpelah right in front of everyone, for ___ price.

cards.text: Abraham's asking the Hittites to go talk to Ephron for him. Ephron? He's sitting RIGHT THERE among them at the gate of his city, with every Hittite listening.

cards.question: With all the Hittites listening at the city gate, what does Ephron tell Abraham?

answers.text: He gives it to Abraham as a gift
He says it isn't for sale

cards.question: Ephron gives Abraham the cave of Machpelah but keeps the field for himself.

cards.text: Again Abraham bows down before the people of the land. Then he turns to Ephron, with everybody watching, and gives his answer.

cards.question: Abraham takes Ephron up on the gift of the field and the cave.

cards.text: Ephron says take it, and Abraham says he's PAYING for it. Friend, this is two people at the register, both waving a card, both yelling, “I GOT IT.”

cards.question: Ephron answers, “Listen to me, my lord.” He says the land is worth four hundred shekels of ___.

cards.text: Then Ephron adds, “but what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.” Friend, somebody once bought ME for twenty-five cents, so four hundred shekels sounds like a WHOLE lot of something to me.

cards.question: Abraham talks Ephron down to a lower price.

cards.text: Abraham weighs out all four hundred shekels of silver, by the standard of the merchants. And Ephron's field at Machpelah near Mamre, the cave in it and every tree inside its boundaries become Abraham's.

cards.question: When Ephron's field and cave are deeded over to Abraham, who is there to see it?

answers.text: All the Hittites at the city gate

cards.text: Then Abraham buries his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre, in the land of Canaan. The man who called himself a foreigner now has a field and a cave deeded to him as a burial site, and friend, Abraham's story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 14 quotes "I GOT IT.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The answers say "He gives it to Abraham as a gift" and "He says it isn't for sale," but nothing in the question says what "it" is. The cave was last named on card 7, which the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Card 14 mostly retells what was already covered. Ephron's offer of the field and cave (v11) was told on cards 10 and 11, and Abraham turning down the gift to pay (v13) was just answered on card 13 and set up on card 8. The register joke rides on a recap instead of on a new moment of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Genesis 23:18 repeats the exact line from 23:10, "in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city." Card 19 asks about it at its second appearance. Cards 9 and 10 already told the baker that every Hittite at the city gate was listening, so the answer is given away. The right answer is also the only group among the choices, which makes it stand out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This card asks about a repeated line at its second appearance instead of its first (Genesis 23:10).

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.
